findings.summary: The page duplicates the established route-segment validator instead of reusing the local navigation helper.
findings.consequence: Future changes to route segment safety rules can drift between this page and internal navigation classification, causing a route to validate here while managed navigation rejects it, or the reverse.
findings.evidence: `validRouteParam` repeats the same length, trim, dot-segment, slash, percent, control-character, and surrogate checks already implemented by `validRouteSegment` in `app/lib/internal-navigation.ts`, which this page already imports from.
findings.recommendation: Import `validRouteSegment` and implement this guard as `typeof value === "string" && validRouteSegment(value, maximum)` so one helper owns the route-segment policy.
verification: Read `app/lib/internal-navigation.ts` and confirmed `validRouteSegment` has the same policy checks.
Inspected `test/unit/internal-navigation.spec.ts` for coverage of the shared validator.

findings.summary: Error-code narrowing relies on a cast after checking a handwritten string list.
findings.consequence: If `AuthorDocumentErrorCode` changes, TypeScript will not force this runtime allow-list to stay synchronized, so a valid backend-local error code could be silently mapped to the generic unavailable state.
findings.evidence: `localCode` checks `nested.code` with an inline string array and then returns `nested.code as AuthorDocumentErrorCode`; the cast is avoidable because the allow-list itself can be typed as the source of truth.
findings.recommendation: Define a typed `ReadonlySet<AuthorDocumentErrorCode>` or a `satisfies readonly AuthorDocumentErrorCode[]` constant and narrow through that helper instead of casting the nested string at the return site.
verification: Read `server/api/author-documents/[author]/[document].get.ts` and `server/utils/author-document.ts` to confirm the emitted local error codes.
